package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code is described in this report. The article discusses general supply chain threats (such as event-stream, Webmin, Browserify typosquatting, and Mimemagic) and how SLSA and Sonatype products address them, but does not provide any actual code snippets or detailed technical analysis of a specific malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Component provenance does not match expected source repository
Unexpected or unauthorized source files in build artifacts
Dependency tree includes packages with suspicious or unverifiable origins
Typosquatting: package names similar to popular packages but with malicious intent
Sudden unavailability or removal of dependencies from public repositories
file_indicators: Packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting)
Build artifacts containing files not present in the source repository
Components with missing or unverifiable provenance metadata
network_indicators: Packages downloaded from untrusted or unofficial mirrors
Unexpected network requests during build or install processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mismatches between component provenance and expected source repositories. Flag packages with names similar to popular libraries (potential typosquatting). Use behavioral analysis to detect suspicious package updates or removals. Employ repository firewalls and component intelligence to quarantine or block components with unverifiable or suspicious origins. Track and alert on unexpected network activity during build or install phases.
